children: Toronto's CD Howe Institute think tank says the Bank of Canada should keep its policy rate unchanged next week, bucking consensus among traders for a quarter-point increase to 2.50%. The institute's monetary-policy panel says Canadian data suggest core CPI remains around the BOC's 2% inflation target, making it "difficult to make the case for a hike." Panel members who advocated for a rate hold add there are major events in coming weeks — such as U.S. midterm results, the federal budget plan, and a Dec. 31 deadline on U.S. auto tariffs — which could influence inflation dynamics and the output gap. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)
